judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact. Every problem on this sheet is a three-part (a)/(b)/(c) item whose (a) and (b) are the classification and the rule, and verification generally reaches only (c): problem 1 asks for the differences and ratios, the linear/exponential verdict, the rule, then f(6) - id 1 is a lone eval (5+3*6 -> 23). The same shape holds for problems 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 10. The demanded explanations are real and unflagged: 3(a) "Say which, in one sentence", 5(b) "Explain in one sentence how it can still end up ahead", 6(c) "What do your two ratios prove about h?", 7(c) "Answer in one sentence", 8(a) "Which description is exponential and which is linear? How do you know?" - and gate_log.txt reports "12 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual". I recomputed every keyed number and all are right: 23, 972, 400, 768, 100*1.5^5-350 = 409.375 -> 409.38, ratios 4 and 2.25, slope (32-17)/(5-2) = 5, 24000*0.88^5-12000 = 665.566 -> 665.57, r=2 with 16000, and 0.01*2^19-1000 = 4242.88.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 is the sheet's best verification design: "neither linear nor exponential" is turned into TWO machine checks (the first ratio 8/2 = 4 and the second 18/8 = 2.25), so the proof that no constant ratio exists is carried by the verifier rather than by prose. That is exactly the reframing SKILL.md asks for, and problem 9 does the same across parts (a) and (b) (r=2, then 16000). The multi-entry shape is already in this file - it just needs to be the rule instead of the exception.

Problem 6 also chooses its numbers well: 2, 8, 18, 32 has first ratio 4 and second 2.25, far enough apart that a student cannot round them together, with second differences of 4 that would tempt a quadratic guess - which is the point of including a "neither" case at all.
Problem 10's doubling-penny scenario is set up to defeat the classic off-by-one: the stem says "Be careful with the exponent: day 1 has been doubled zero times", and the check is 0.01*2^19, not 2^20.

The three declared traps each encode the canonical linear/exponential confusion with derived numbers - 100*1.5*5 (multiplying once then by 5), 24000*(1-0.12*5) (treating percent decay as a fixed fraction of the ORIGINAL), 0.01*2*19 - and each prints as a grading sentence in the key.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's verification contract has a per-PROBLEM floor, not a per-RESPONSE-SLOT floor: "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". A multi-part sheet therefore satisfies the gate with one scalar per id, and build.sh prints "0 manual" - which reads as "everything on this sheet was checked" rather than "every id had something checked". On this sheet every problem has three printed parts and most carry one entry, so the classification and the rule - the two things the focus "distinguishing exponential from linear change" actually names - sit outside the boundary while the arithmetic that follows them sits inside it.
evidence: problem 1 "(a) Write the differences ... Which one is constant? (b) Is f linear or exponential? Write its rule. (c) Find f(6)." -- id 1 is a lone eval (23)
problems 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 10 repeat that shape with one entry each
verify.json ids 6 and 9 DO carry two entries apiece, so the shape is available in the same file
the worksheet directions: "For every table, write the difference row and the ratio row before deciding" -- neither row is ever checked

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says it plainly - "Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer" - but line 249 immediately narrows it ("Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning") and tells the author to reframe error analysis "via the ordinary types". Read together, the guidance reads as a licence to type an explanation-bearing problem by its numeric half. Nothing in the gate chain notices, because no gate reads the problem prose looking for a demanded explanation.
evidence: problem 3(a): "Is the balance changing by a constant difference or a constant ratio? Say which, in one sentence."
problem 5(b): "Plan E is behind Plan L at step 1. Explain in one sentence how it can still end up ahead."
problem 7(c): "If instead the pattern were exponential through those same two points, would the rate of change still be constant? Answer in one sentence."
problem 8(a): "Which description is exponential and which is linear? How do you know?"
verify.json contains no manual entry; gate_log.txt: "12 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual"

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three documents only by role ("the student worksheet (6 pages), a step-by-step answer key, and a two-page skills summary") with no filename or path anywhere in its 102 lines, although gate_log.txt printed all three.
evidence: final_response.md contains no ".pdf", "ws_", "ak_" or "ss_" token and no output path
SKILL.md step 6: "report the three output paths clearly"
eight of the ten cases in this batch do print the three filenames

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule in SKILL.md from "every id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed response slot has a check", and enforce it mechanically: add a slot counter to tests/check_layout.py (which already parses the worksheet .tex for answer-location macros) that counts, per problem, the lettered parts ((a)/(b)/(c)), the blank cells of a fill-in table, and each answer line, then reports when a problem's verify entries number fewer than its slots. Multi-entry ids are already legal and already used in these same files, so the fix adds entries, not machinery.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 prints "(a) ... (b) ... (c) ..." with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry for id 2. Assert the gate chain flags problem 2 with the two uncovered parts named. Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims full verification.
improvements.expected_impact: Multi-part problems stop being certified on the strength of their last line. Across this batch the same shape appears in curr-252, curr-256, curr-275, curr-276 and curr-300.
improvements.risk: Medium: counting slots from .tex will over-count where a lettered part is rhetorical rather than a response. Ship as exit 2 (manual visibility) before promoting to exit 1, so a correct build is never blocked by a parse artefact.

improvements.title: Classification-and-justification parts must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so a stem that asks the student to CLASSIFY and say how they know gets a `manual` entry beside its numeric check, and add the prose lint in tests/check_layout.py for "how do you know", "say which", "explain in one sentence", "what do your ... prove". Here that is manual entries on ids 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8; each desc already exists as prose in answer_key.pdf. Where the classification itself is closed-form (linear vs exponential vs neither), prefer the stronger fix - an eval or compare check on the constant difference/ratio, as problem 6 already does - and reserve manual for the "how do you know" half.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 reads "(a) Is it linear or exponential? How do you know? (b) Find f(6)" with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 2. Assert the build exits 2 with problem 2 listed manual; today it exits 0 with "0 manual".
improvements.expected_impact: The five written justifications become visible to the grader and the sheet stops reporting a concept-models worksheet, whose whole subject is the classification, as fully machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over problem prose will fire on stems that use "explain" inside a hint rather than as a demand. Ship it as exit 2 (manual-review visibility), which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: Delivery text names the three documents only by role, never by filename or path
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md step 6 says to "report the three output paths clearly". Make that mechanical rather than advisory: have build.sh's final summary emit a copy-ready delivery block containing the three PDF paths it already prints under its PDFs heading, and state in SKILL.md step 6 that the delivery message must reproduce those three paths verbatim.
improvements.regression_test: Harness check over evals/runs/*/tasks/*/final_response.md asserting each contains all three PDF basenames printed in that task's gate_log.txt PDFs block. It fails today for this case and passes once the delivery text quotes them.
improvements.expected_impact: A reader of the delivery message can tell which of the three files is which and where to find them, matching the eight other cases in this batch that do print the ws_/ak_/ss_ names.
improvements.risk: Low. Purely additive to the delivery text; no artefact or gate behaviour changes.

case_summary: Strong concept-models teaching: one governing question ("is the step an addition or a multiplication?") runs through all ten problems, problem 6 supplies a genuine "neither" case whose two ratios (4 and 2.25) are BOTH machine-checked, problem 10's stem pre-empts the day-1 exponent off-by-one, and three derived traps encode the canonical confusions. Every one of the twelve keyed numbers is correct under independent recomputation. The rejection is right: each problem prints three parts, the classification and the rule are parts (a) and (b), and most ids carry a single check on part (c) - so the sheet's actual subject sits outside verification, while five demanded one-sentence explanations ship under a "0 manual" build. The fix needs no new machinery: ids 6 and 9 in this same file already carry two entries each. One finding the judge did not raise: final_response.md never names a filename or path for any of the three PDFs.
